title: AI Got Better While I Was Away. Software Didn't.
why_read: An opinion piece arguing AI-assisted coding has sped up code generation without fixing underlying software engineering judgment problems, more reflective than technical.
analysis: This is a personal essay arguing that while AI coding tools have gotten much better at generating code quickly, the harder engineering problems like deciding what should be built or whether complexity is warranted remain unsolved. It's a reasonably common sentiment in current developer discourse, framed with casual rhetorical style rather than new data or evidence. Readers looking for fresh technical insight won't find much beyond a relatable but familiar argument.
